To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the onset of viral DNA synthesis in MVM-infected cells coincides with that of cellular DNA synthesis and that the overall rate of viral DNA synthesis does not decrease the overall rate of cellular DNA synthesis in MvM-infected cells because it is compensated by concomitance viral DNA synthesis.

(i) cellular and viral DNA synthesis occur simultaneously in infected cells; (ii) the inhibition of cellular DNA synthesis by MVM is compensated by viral DNA synthesis; and (iii) viral DNA replication is driven by a cellular DNA polymerase.
MVM DNA replication is highly dependent on host cell DNA synthesis, and that the virus is assembled during the late phase of viral DNA replication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interrelationship between viral and cellular functions during MVM infection.

the interrelations between viral and host DNA synthesis in mouse fibroblasts infected with the parvo virus minute virus of mice and the role of cellular DNA polymerase α in the DNA replication of autonomous viruses.
the interrelations between viral and cellular replication in cells arrested in G0 and released into the cell cycle by MVM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in mouse cells MVM infection induces a block to cellular DNA synthesis and a reduction in the amount of cellular DNA replicated.
the DNA synthesis of MVM and of its host is carried out by the same cellular machinery, namely DNA polymerase alpha.

, in mouse cells infected by MVM, viral DNA synthesis and cellular DNA synthesis are interdependent, and that the overall rate of viral DNA replication is determined by the rate of DNA synthesis of the host cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, at least in mouse fibroblasts, the DNA replication of autonomous MVM requires the participation of cellular DNA polymerase(s) and the presence of cellular factor(s) which are only available to the virus when the cells are in S phase.
the autonomous parvovoirus minute virus of mouse is an efficient inhibitor of cell proliferation.
the autonomous parvovoirus MVM replicates its DNA in the host nucleus by utilizing a host DNA polymerase, probably the alpha enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the replication of MVM DNA is highly coordinated with that of cellular DNA and that the two events are dependent on the same cellular factor(s).
the DNA synthesis of MVM and its host cell is tightly linked, and the virus does not seem to interfere with cellular DNA synthesis.
MVM and host DNA replication are tightly coupled and are dependent on the same cellular factors.
